primaryWitness.text: Where are the gods of Hamath and of Arpad? Where are the gods of Sepharvaim, of Hena, and Ivvah? Have they delivered Samaria out of my hand?

wiki.title: Arpad, Syria
wiki.supportSummary: The article identifies Arpad as an ancient Aramaean/Neo-Hittite city in north-west Syria, lists 2 Kings 18:34 and 19:13, and says the Rabshakeh names its gods in the speech; Tell Rifaat as site remains qualified as “probably.”

primaryWitness.text: Now the rest of the acts of Jeroboam, and all that he did, and his might, how he fought, and how he recovered Damascus, and Hamath, which had belonged to Judah, for Israel, aren’t they written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?

wiki.title: Hama
wiki.supportSummary: The article’s Biblical section treats Hamath as the ancient kingdom/city and discusses its biblical history; it cites other Kings references and describes Solomon’s possession, so the article is relevant to the ancient Hamath referent but its later events must not be carried into the 14:28 first-appearance note.
